A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical debugging framework, renamed from FixAgent to UniDebugger. The main text, tables, figures, Algorithm 1, and appendices A.1–A.4 are readable and can be matched despite extensive appendix reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original debugging experiments on four benchmarks, comparisons across LLM backbones, agent and tool ablations, and worked repair cases.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark results, backbone comparisons, ablations, and appendix repair cases.

M1.justification: The seven agents, three repair levels, tool interactions, refinement procedure, Algorithm 1, and appendix prompts are retained. The less specific description of Lite and the new explanation of diff-format editing do not establish an actual procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Defects4J, Codeflaws, QuixBugs, and ConDefects with the same programming languages and repair tasks. SWE-bench and issue-driven repair are newly discussed, but neither is newly evaluated.

E2.justification: The 14 APR baselines and other LLM comparators match. However, Tables 1 and 3 relabel DeepSeekCoder as DeepSeekCoderV2 while retaining its citation and every score. The PDFs do not clarify whether this corrects the identifier or represents an evaluated model replacement.

E3.justification: The metrics, dataset selections, 600 ConDefects samples, 100-patch correctness checks, and five/20-attempt budgets are retained. The newly stated one-second query timeout is a disclosure, not an explicit revision. Whether the DeepSeekCoderV2 label denotes a changed backbone setting remains unresolved.

E4.justification: The backbone comparison, agent ablations, and external-interaction ablations in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. Appendices A.1 and A.4 retain the same unique-fix example and Lang-1 execution case; their enlarged illustrations provide no new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No seed information or uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain all numerical values, including repair counts, correctness rates, gains, and costs. Both report 197 correct and 286 plausible Defects4J fixes, 3,130 plausible Codeflaws fixes, and 40 correct QuixBugs fixes per language. The overlap diagram and appendix findings are also unchanged; the DeepSeek identifier ambiguity is addressed under E2/E3.

T1.justification: The hierarchical assumptions, cognitive-model foundation, and correctness-rate definition are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the new CI/CD and patch-format explanations introduce no mathematical development.

C1.justification: The introduction refines the broad unified-debugging framing into developer-side, test-driven debugging and adds a claim of seamless CI/CD integration. The central hierarchical multi-agent contribution and abstract/conclusion performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 substantially replaces its limitations: v2 discusses coordination overhead, fixed-role generalization, and tool-integration delays; v3 instead explains the test-driven applicability boundary, requirements for extending to issue-driven repair, and unknown effectiveness on configuration errors. Section 3.2 also adds a training-format rationale for diff-based editing relative to Search/Replace.

D1.justification: v3 newly states a one-second query timeout, adds API-access and tool-license disclosures in Artifact Discussion, and changes the advertised code repository account from AcceptePapier to BEbillionaireUSD. It also drops the explicit three-agent enumeration for Lite. Existing pseudocode and detailed prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to SWE-bench, Agentless, and Motwani et al.'s repair-quality study. These support a new distinction between developer-oriented test-driven repair and user-reported issues, plus a comparison of patch-editing formats; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The framework is renamed throughout, introductory paragraphs are reorganized, the LLM discussion is merged into multi-agent related work, and Artifact Discussion and acknowledgments are added. Section 6 is rewritten, while most method, experiment, and appendix prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands from a small column-width display to a full-width table. The appendix switches to a single-column layout with substantially enlarged pseudocode, prompts, and execution illustrations, often on separate pages. v2's generic system-prompt illustration, Figure 3, is removed; the other figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the test-driven applicability boundary clearer and substantially improves the readability of Table 3 and the appendix material. These are useful gains without stronger experimental evidence. The removal of practical limitations and unexplained DeepSeek model label temper the improvement, so the overall benefit is limited.
